method.name: milp_training_allocation
steps: Define integer decision variables: t1 = number of jets allocated to training in year 1 (0..10), t2 = number of jets allocated to training in year 2 (0..15).
Each training jet produces 5 pilots per year. Year 1 jets train for 2 years, so by end of year 2 they produce 5*t1*2 = 10*t1 pilots.
Year 2 jets start training in year 2; after 1 year they have 5*t2 pilots HALF-trained (not fully trained until year 3).
Year 1 combat jets = 10 - t1. Year 2 combat jets = 15 - t2.
Trained pilots from year 1 (50 total) operate year 2 combat jets. Constraint: 15 - t2 <= 50, i.e., t2 >= -35 (always satisfied).
Year 1 combat jets (10-t1) need pilots from year 0 (none exist). So all year 1 jets must train: t1 = 10.
Thus t1=10, t2 in [0,15]. Fully trained pilots by end of year 2 = 5*t1*2 = 100. But this counts 50 pilots who finished at end of year 1 plus 50 more at end of year 2 = 50 cumulative increase.
By end of year 2: 50 pilots trained in year 1 (fully trained) are available for combat. Year 2 training cohort not yet ready.
Total fully trained pilots available by end of year 2 = 50 (from year 1 cohort).
Alternative interpretation: total trained (including partial) = 50 + 5*t2. With t2=15 (all jets train): 50 + 75 = 125.
Given the problem asks for 'how many trained pilots will be available', and training takes 2 years, only year 1 cohort is fully trained: answer = 50.

method.name: milp_time_indexed_production
steps: Define decision variables for each month t: produce[t] (in-house units), outsource[t] (outsourced units), hire[t] (workers hired), fire[t] (workers fired), workforce[t] (end-of-month workforce), inv[t] (end-of-month inventory), bo[t] (end-of-month backorders), sell[t] (units sold).
All production/outsourcing/inventory/worker variables are integer (non-negative).
Workforce dynamics: workforce[t] = workforce[t-1] + hire[t] - fire[t] (January starts at 1000).
Labor capacity: produce[t] * 5 <= workforce[t] * 160 + workforce[t] * 20 (regular+overtime hours).
Inventory balance: inv[t] = inv[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t] - sell[t] (January starts at 15000).
Backorder balance: bo[t] = bo[t-1] + demand[t] - sell[t] (January starts at 0).
Sales bound: sell[t] <= inv[t-1] + produce[t] + outsource[t] + bo[t-1] (cannot sell more than available).
Terminal: inv['Jun'] >= 10000, bo['Jun'] = 0.

Revenue = 300 * sum(sell[t]); costs: raw material 90*produce[t], outsourcing 200*outsource[t], holding 15*inv[t], backorder 35*bo[t], regular wage 30*160*workforce[t], overtime 40*overtime_hours[t], hiring 5000*hire[t], firing 8000*fire[t]. Overtime hours = max(0, produce[t]*5 - workforce[t]*160) but <= workforce[t]*20.
Maximize total net profit = revenue - all costs.
